title: A bounded graph of the pack: sources, measurements and entities, with counted edges
problem: A reader has no way to see the shape of a pack — which sources feed it, what kinds of measurement they hold, and which recorded names those measurements attach to — without asking one question at a time. The consumer must not infer relationships client-side (that is the id-verification boundary from IDL-REQ-0002/TR-VIS-0003), and pulling raw rows to assemble edges in the browser is the wrong shape at 42k records. What is missing is one bounded, aggregated view of the pack as a graph.
evidence: Everything the graph needs already exists producer-side in aggregate form: audit.source_versions, the estimate target catalogue (source → quantities with count columns), site-orientation denominators, the bounded entity catalogue with per-entity record counts (subject_resolver), and declared entity↔entity pairs (interaction-pairs, 5,622 named frugivory pairs).

The consumer's data explorer already renders source → quantity lists from /v1/estimate/targets; it cannot show which entities those quantities attach to, or how entities relate, because no endpoint aggregates that.

The UX (a full-page 'Atlas' under Data) is built and shipping against the fixture in dss/contracts/fixtures/graph/ — the fixture is the acceptance shape; a labelled sample-data fallback renders until this endpoint exists.
requested_outcome: GET /v1/graph — an overview payload (schema idli-graph/1, fixture dss/contracts/fixtures/graph/overview.json): node_kinds (kind, human label, total count), nodes (id, kind, label, records, plus kind-specific counts such as sources-per-entity), edges (from, to, records), and a `more` object counting what the caps omitted. Entities capped to top-N by records (producer chooses N ≤ ~30); sources and measurement kinds are small enough to send whole.

GET /v1/graph/node/{id} — a focus payload (fixture graph/node-*.json): the node, its neighbors grouped by a `relation` word (recorded_in, measures, interacts_with, member_of — plain machine keys the consumer maps to producer-provided labels), each neighbor with edge counts, capped per relation with an `omitted` count, and idli-result/1-shaped `actions` for click-through (e.g. entity-record-map for an entity node).

GET /v1/graph?q=<text> — bounded entity search over recorded names/aliases returning matching entity nodes (same node shape), so the '…and 949 more' fold resolves through search rather than a full dump.

All labels are the pack's own human words (source titles, humanised quantity names, recorded names) — no sector vocabulary is assumed by the consumer, so the same screen serves the ecology and livelihoods packs unchanged.
Counts are honest aggregates of admitted records (same audit basis as site-orientation denominators); a node with thin data should look thin.
Cheap to serve: precomputable at pack index time; an ETag or pack_digest field so the consumer can cache per pack version.
acceptance: The overview fixture shape renders live: sources → measurement kinds → top entities with counted ribbons for both the ecology and livelihoods packs, no consumer code change.
Focusing an entity returns its sources with per-source record counts, its measurement kinds, and (ecology pack) its declared interaction partners — each expandable by a further node call.
graph?q=hornbill returns the hornbill entities with counts; a term matching nothing returns an empty list, not an error.
Every count equals what the corresponding capability reports (e.g. an entity's records total matches entity-record-map's denominator).
A pack without declared entity↔entity pairs simply omits that relation — the consumer renders whatever relations arrive.
notes: The graph is an index, not an analysis engine: clicking a node in the Atlas seeds the mapped question through the conversation, so insight still flows through audited turns. The consumer renders exactly the nodes/edges/labels supplied and never invents membership — same boundary as subject resolution.
